input.reason: The two things that make the watchlist hard to use today are that it can only be read as one flat list (no way to see what is still unwatched or find a title) and that removing an item is irreversible. I will make it easier to scan (filter tabs + sort options surfaced through a new computed visibleMovies) and safer to edit (undo for remove, backed by a new persisted WatchlistStore.restore). All changes are additive; existing behaviour and tests stay intact.

steps.instruction: Add a public `restore(item: WatchItem): void` method that backs an undo-remove feature on the watchlist page. Behaviour: (1) if an item with the same id is already on the list, restore is a no-op — no duplicate, no overwrite, no reordering; (2) otherwise append the exact WatchItem passed in (id, title, watched, poster_path, release_date kept unchanged, watched state included) to the end of the items list; (3) persist the change with the same localStorage mechanism that add/remove already use, so a restored item survives a page reload; (4) keep the existing signals consistent (items, count, watchedCount — watchedCount only increases when the restored item has watched === true). Do not change add/remove/toggleWatched or any existing exported declaration; all existing tests must keep passing.
steps.interfaceChange:
restore(item: WatchItem): void;

// WatchItem is already imported by watchlist-store; no other new declarations.

steps.instruction: Make the watchlist page easier to scan and safer to edit, purely additively (all existing exported members and tests must keep working). Add: (1) Filtering — `filter: Signal<WatchlistFilter>` defaulting to 'all' and `setFilter(filter: WatchlistFilter): void`; a computed `visibleMovies: Signal<WatchItem[]>` starts from `movies()` and keeps only: 'all' → everything, 'unwatched' → watched === false, 'watched' → watched === true. (2) Sorting — `sort: Signal<WatchlistSort>` defaulting to 'added' and `setSort(sort: WatchlistSort): void`, applied after filtering inside visibleMovies: 'added' → keep the current store order; 'title' → alphabetical A→Z by title, case-insensitive; 'release' → release_date descending (newest first), items without a release_date go last. (3) Undo removal — `lastRemoved: Signal<WatchItem | null>` defaulting to null and `undoRemove(): void`. `remove(movie)` keeps its current behaviour and additionally sets lastRemoved to the item that was removed. `undoRemove()`: when lastRemoved() is non-null, call the NEW method `this.store.restore(lastRemoved())` (WatchlistStore is being extended this round with exactly `restore(item: WatchItem): void` — it appends the exact item back, preserves the watched state, persists it, and is a no-op if the id is already present), then set lastRemoved back to null and update `announcement` so screen-reader users hear that the item was re-added; when lastRemoved() is null, undoRemove() must do nothing. (4) Template — render the movie rows from visibleMovies() instead of movies(); add UI controls wired to setFilter (All / Unwatched / Watched) and setSort (Recently added / Title / Release date) with the active choice visibly indicated; show an undo affordance (e.g. a button calling undoRemove()) only while lastRemoved() is non-null; show a short friendly message when visibleMovies() is empty (e.g. when a filter hides everything); update the announcement messages for filter/sort changes so they are announced via the existing aria-live mechanism. Exact UI copy is your choice except where behaviour is pinned by the acceptance test.

content.text: I'll add the `restore` method to the store and add tests covering the four behaviours.
